title: Having a hard time creating a base avatar with Astra
author: laziokid
selftext:
Hey all, somewhat new to the vibe coding scene and I’m trying to make a base avatar for an 2.5D isometric game (personal project) with different layers (clothes, glasses, shoes, etc.). This is important because I plan to release new clothes and such overtime that will fit on the same base model character. Has anyone had any luck with this? The closest one it almost nailed looked like a Roblox character but I’m going more for an anime vibe. Looking for all 8 directions so the character can wave, sit, etc.   
is this too complicated for Astra to create?

comments.author: TheRealLunicuss
comments.body:
Yeah to be fair almost all the character work I've seen Astra do has looked like that. I feel like most of the work I've seen from Astra all looks like the same, kind of like an artist's signature, the closer to a one-shot prompt the more of the signature is present. So I think you might need to just get ultra specific to avoid that generic Astra Roblox look.

Are you actually working in 3d and just locking an orthographic camera perspective or is it actually 2d?

replies.author: laziokid
replies.body: Thanks for the reply! 2D- There's no camera anywhere in it, and nothing is rendered in three dimensions. I even tried uploading sample images and it nails the front view, but then the avatar walks funny where the sides are slimmer, if that makes sense. The clothing layers also do not sit properly. Not sure what I’m doing wrong

replies.author: TheRealLunicuss
replies.body: I've tried a good many approaches trying to solve the exact same problem of how to handle equipment in a 2d isometric setting. It's a really hard problem. I take it you're using a paper doll approach where Astra has created a 2d isometric sprite and then split it into body parts for an animation rig?

replies.body:
